front: How do social science passages differ from humanities passages?
why: Genre contrast is context; evidence-evaluation tactic lives on other cards

front: How do you handle passages presenting competing theories?
why: Tracking which theory the author endorses is needed on nearly every such passage

front: How should you evaluate a cited study in a passage?
why: Study-evaluation (sample, design vs conclusion) is directly tested research reasoning

front: What does it mean when an author says a finding is "suggestive"?
why: Hedge words decide certainty-matching, a trap on nearly every passage

front: What is the most common reasoning flaw tested in these passages?
why: Correlation-vs-causation and confounding are tested every year across sections

front: What should you do when a passage presents statistics?
why: Statistic-misdescription is a real but secondary trap

front: What subjects fall under social science CARS passages?
Why is scope especially important in social science passages?
why: Overgeneralized scope is one of the most common wrong-answer patterns
